_README: Definitions for which the ledger holds BOTH an agreeing and a disagreeing
verdict. A definition cannot be validated and falsified at once: one of the
designs is wrong, or the two are measuring different regimes, and the
`ledger` guard in check.py fails until this file says which and why.
`authoritative` names the battery whose verdict stands. `superseded` lists
the batteries whose verdicts do not, each with the defect that explains it.
A superseded verdict is not deleted -- the record stays in ledger.json and
the reason travels with it, because a design fault that produced a wrong
verdict once will produce it again unless it is written down.

reason: The two surviving designs agree and together they locate a REGIME rather
than a defect. `r2_target = rho^2 * h2_target` while `r2Source = h2_source`,
so `r2Source * rhoSq` is exact only when the two populations have equal
heritability. bulk41b rescales the drawn target effect vector to the source
vector's norm, which holds the two heritabilities equal, and matches at 2.34
sems. bulk39 does not rescale, so the two heritabilities differ by the
sampling scatter in the vector norms -- O(1/sqrt(m)) = 3.5% at m = 800 -- and
resolves a 1.2 to 2.7 percent residual at 9.19 sems on 400000 individuals.
bulk41b's own UNEQUAL-heritability cells show the same sign at 1.05 percent
and 2.51 sems, which its smaller m and n could not resolve. Neither battery
is wrong; the body needs the equal-heritability condition stated, and it now
is.

bulk22: Two design faults, either sufficient to produce the 353-sem falsification.
It evaluated the prediction at the NOMINAL genetic correlation while m = 400
effect vectors have a realised correlation about 5% away, which at
n = 200000 is hundreds of sems. And it built the target phenotype as
gt + N(0, sqrt(max(1 - Var gt, 1e-6))), so at alpha = 1.6 the genetic
variance is 1.28, the residual clamped to zero, and the target R-squared
jumped to 0.82 against a prediction of 0.43.
bulk41: Fixed the nominal-rho fault and inherited the clamped-residual one, so its
490-sem falsification is the alpha != 1 cells alone.

reason: The two designs disagree because they move `alpha` by different means, and
that difference IS the convention the docstring was missing. bulk39 produces
the score-scale ratio by rescaling the WEIGHTS, which moves alpha while
leaving the target phenotype on its own scale; there the `1/alpha` factor is
real and the body matches at 6.80 sems with the variance-ratio reading
rejected at 103 sems on the same cells. bulk41b produces it by rescaling the
GENOTYPES and scales the target residual with the resulting genetic variance,
so the phenotype is standardized too, covariance and variance both pick up
alpha squared, and the factor cancels exactly -- the measured slope is
rho * bSource with no alpha at all, 0.900 against rho = 0.8987.
So bulk41b did not falsify the body; it measured a construction in which
alpha is not a free parameter. The finding it produced stands and is the
reason this entry exists: two conventions were written down -- sd ratio
versus variance ratio -- and a third, what happens to the OUTCOME scale, was
not, and the third is the one that decides the answer.

bulk22: Evaluated the prediction at the nominal genetic correlation rather than the
realised one, which at m = 400 and n = 200000 is worth hundreds of sems on
its own, and clamped the target residual at alpha != 1.
bulk41: Fixed the nominal-rho fault and inherited the clamped-residual one.
bulk41b: Not a defect in the design: it measures the genotype-rescaling convention,
under which alpha cancels and the body's alpha factor is not on trial. Its
cells are correct for what they measure and say nothing about bulk39's.

reason: The MATCH and the FALSIFIED are both from battery_mi01 and they are not in
conflict: they are the two halves of a bound, and recording only one would
be the misreading.
Under GAUSSIAN dependence the body is the mutual information, measured
against a Kraskov-Stogbauer-Grassberger estimator that assumes no density
model -- worst 1.75 sems, 0.94% relative -- with the factor m in place of
m/2 refuted at 386 sems and log(1-rho) in place of log(1-rho^2) at 148.
OFF that family the same body is a strict LOWER BOUND, because at fixed
correlation the Gaussian is the maximum-entropy joint and therefore the
minimum-information one. Cells with a randomised coupling at the SAME
realised rho exceed it by 53%, 27% and 109%, and in the cell where the
coupling is symmetric about zero the correlation vanishes, the body
predicts no information, and the estimator finds 2.14 nats.
So the FALSIFIED row is not a defect in the design and not a rival to the
MATCH. It is the measurement of the condition, and it is what makes the
check able to fail: had the body matched non-Gaussian dependence it would
have been refuted as a claim about mutual information at all.

reason: bulk29 matches at 3.51 sems and 1.21 percent, with the competing reading
`h2 * r` unsquared rejected at 652 sems on the same cells, so the match is
gated. The falsifications it displaces are the nominal-versus-realised
heritability trap, and battery dis1 demonstrates that directly: on one set
of cells the `nominal h2` reading is a LEAD at 6.67 sems while the
`realised h2` reading matches at 1.19 sems.

bulk5: 42-sem falsification with NO competing formula carried, so it could not
show the design was capable of rejecting anything, and it fed nominal h2.
bulk7: Recorded LEAD, not a falsification: it carried no positive control, so by
the harness's own rule the disagreement was never a finding.

reason: Both designs simulate the infinite-alleles equilibrium and they disagree
because they estimate HETEROZYGOSITY differently, not because they disagree
about the body. `battery_ia02` computes `1 - sum p_i^2` over the WHOLE
sample with the unbiased n/(n-1) correction and never conditions on
polymorphism, sweeps theta a hundredfold -- over which the three candidate
readings separate by up to a factor of two -- and carries a positive control
that is independent of every body under test (Ewens' E(K)), which passes at
0.33 sems. The body matches at worst 0.68 sems.
`battery_pgs`'s `test_het_mutation_floor` does neither. It takes
`1 - sum f^2` from the raw sample frequencies, so the estimate is biased
low by (n-1)/n; and it averages per SITE over the sites a replicate happens
to carry, so sites with no mutation contribute nothing and the average is
conditioned on polymorphism -- which inflates heterozygosity exactly where
theta is small and the two readings separate. It declares no control. Its
11.6 sems is the size of those two estimator faults, not of an error in
`bulk20`'s VOID and `bulk20b`'s UNINFORMATIVE are not in conflict with
either: neither asserts anything.

reason: The two records are about DIFFERENT FORMULAS, which is why they can both be
right. `battery_transfer` falsified `exp(-2 * recomb * t_div)` at 13.09 sems
and +10.8% relative, with the error growing in `recomb` exactly as the gap
between an exponential and `(1-r)^(2t)` requires. That falsification is what
MOVED the body: DGP.lean now reads `(1 - recomb)^(2 * t_div)`.
`battery_sld03` put the corrected body back to the identical design -- same
three (r, t) cells, same 400000 replicates, same oracle, an ancestral
haplotype surviving t meioses without recombination as an exact Bernoulli
count -- and it matches. It also re-rejects the superseded exponential and
the ploidy-dropped `(1-r)^t` on the same cells, so the exponent's factor of
two is measured rather than named.
The ledger files `transfer`'s row as a corpus row because it was bare-named
when it ran, and at that moment it WAS the corpus body. The record stays,
with this note, because a superseded verdict about a superseded body is
history and not an error.

transfer: Transcribes `exp(-2 * recomb * t_div)`, which is not the body in DGP.lean.
Its falsification is correct and is the reason the body changed.

reason: The two runs are in DIFFERENT REGIMES and both are correct about the one
they are in. The body is `pi*(1-pi)*(1 - r2)`, which is the Brier score of a
calibrated probability on the OBSERVED scale: p has mean pi and variance
r2*pi*(1-pi), the outcome is Bernoulli(p), and the realised mean squared
error is exactly that expression. `battery_falsrepair` group D simulates
that regime directly and matches at 1.18 sems, with the liability-scale form
refuted at 107 sems and the squared-factor reading at 118 on the same cells.
`battery_bulk33` thresholds a latent signal to prevalence pi and scores the
CALIBRATED conditional probability given the signal. That is the liability
threshold model, in which `vSignal` and `vResidual` are liability variances
and the Brier score is `pi - Phi_2(z, z; r2)` -- a different function, which
battery_falsrepair carries as the competitor and which is the one bulk33's
design actually measures. Its 299 sems is the gap between two regimes, not
an error in either formula.
What this costs the reader is stated rather than hidden: the body has no
argument that says which scale its variances are on, so a consumer who feeds
it liability variances gets bulk33's answer and not this one.

bulk33: Measures the liability-threshold regime, where the calibrated Brier score is
`pi - Phi_2(z, z; r2)` and not `pi*(1-pi)*(1-r2)`. The verdict is about a
different quantity, and battery_falsrepair carries that quantity explicitly.

reason: The two verdicts are about two different formulas, and the falsification is
the reason the body changed. `battery_bulk38` transcribed
`1/(1 + theta + bigM)` and rejected it at 3.30 sems and 57% relative on a
two-deme island model under infinite alleles. DGP.lean now reads
`1/(1 + theta + 2*bigM)`: the migration term carries the deme-count
correction `islandDemeCorrection`, which at d = 2 is a factor of two, and
which the corpus had already measured and installed under that name.
Two independent runs put the CORRECTED body back on designs the old one
failed. `battery_bulk38b` re-runs bulk38's own cells -- same estimator, same
Ne, both forces at order one -- and matches at 1.03 sems while rejecting the
superseded body at 3.30, the multiplicative composition at 3.01, and the two
one-force readings at 7.97 and 28.00. `battery_falsrepair` group A repeats it
at new seeds with two extra migration cells and a per-replicate F_ST, and
matches at 1.10 sems.
`battery_transfer`'s row is UNINFORMATIVE and asserts nothing either way.

bulk38: Transcribes `1/(1 + theta + bigM)`, which is not the body in DGP.lean.
Its falsification is correct and is what moved the body to carry the
deme correction on the migration term.

reason: Same body, same twenty demes, same estimator, and the two runs differ in ONE
thing: `falsrepair` group C uses `simlib.island_fst`, which sets
`recombination_rate = 0`, so each replicate is a single genealogy;
`falsrepair_c2` simulates 2 Mb at 1e-8 so each replicate averages over many.
That is a difference in POWER and not in regime. c2's error bars are roughly
half the size at twice the replicate count, and the sweep is filled in from
three cells to five.
At those bars the many-deme body `1/(1 + 4*Ne*m + 4*Ne*mu)` misses by 3.92
sems and 13% relative, while the FINITE-deme form carrying the d/(d-1)
correction -- `1/(1 + 4*Ne*m*(20/19) + 4*Ne*mu)` -- matches at 2.47 on the
same cells, and the two-deme form is rejected at 17.11. group C's MATCH at
1.57 sems is the same measurement through an error bar too wide to separate
the two, which is what a one-genealogy design buys.
So the finding is that the deme correction is visible at d = 20 and the
many-deme LIMIT is not the right body at that deme count. The corpus already
carries the corrected form under `fstIslandEquilibriumFiniteDemes`; what this
entry records is that the limit's own marker cannot claim a validation off
the weaker design.
